newsitem.title: UK: Burmah Castrol reports 10 pct profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Burmah Castrol reports 10 pct profit rise.

text.p: Lubricants maker Burmah Castrol Plc on Monday reported a 10 percent rise in its 1996 profit, which came in higher than analysts had expected.

Profit after tax before exceptional items rose to 148.7 million pounds ($243 million), up from 135.0 million the previous year. But Burmah added growth this year would be more significantly restricted than in 1996 if the pound remained at current high levels.
Burmah said the pound's strength had a negative impact of 3.4 million pounds on 1996 results, but added that this was offset by tax savings of 6.3 million.
The company posted strong growth in the Asia Pacific as well as other developing regions such as the Middle East, Eastern and Central Europe and Latin America.
There were, however, more difficult trading conditions in mature European and North American markets.
Burmah said it wants to support its lubricants and chemical business through investments and acquisitions, but added it did not expect sizeable purchases at the moment. ($1=.6120 Pound)
